Philosophy Quotes About Happiness

Happiness in philosophy often means flourishing (eudaimonia) rather than a fleeting mood. These quotations ask what kind of life is worth wanting, and which goods are stable enough to count as happiness.

Quotes / About / Happiness

27 quotations on happiness

  1. The human good is activity of soul in accordance with virtue.
    Aristotle
    Happiness
  2. Pleasure is the beginning and end of the happy life — not the pleasures of profligates, but freedom from pain in the body and from disturbance in the soul.
    Epicurus
    Life
  3. Of all that wisdom provides for the happiness of a whole life, by far the greatest is the possession of friendship.
    Epicurus
    Friendship
  4. It is better to be a human being dissatisfied than a pig satisfied; better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied.
    John Stuart Mill
    Happiness
  5. The struggle itself toward the heights is enough to fill a man's heart. One must imagine Sisyphus happy.
    Albert Camus
    Philosophy
  6. The secret of happiness is this: let your interests be as wide as possible, and let your reactions…be as far as possible friendly rather than hostile.
    Bertrand Russell
    Happiness
  7. To abandon the struggle for private happiness…to burn with passion for eternal things — this is emancipation.
    Bertrand Russell
    Philosophy
  8. Next to worry, probably one of the most potent causes of unhappiness is envy.
    Bertrand Russell
    Philosophy
  9. Envy is itself a terrible obstacle to happiness.
    Bertrand Russell
    Philosophy
  10. The Master said: Is it not a pleasure to learn and to practice what one has learned in due time? Is it not a joy to have friends come from afar? Is it not the mark of a gentleman to remain unresentful when others fail to appreciate one?
    Confucius
    Learning
  11. It is the greatest happiness of the greatest number that is the measure of right and wrong.
    Jeremy Bentham
    Happiness
  12. I say that the noble and good man and woman are happy, and the unjust and wicked are miserable.
    Plato
    Happiness
  13. For one swallow does not make a spring, nor does one day.
    Aristotle
    Happiness
  14. It is perhaps also strange to make the happy person a solitary.
    Aristotle
    Friendship
  15. Felicity is a continual progress of the desire, from one object to another.
    Thomas Hobbes
    Desire
  16. One must imagine Sisyphus happy.
    Albert Camus
    Philosophy
  17. All things are already complete in me. There is no greater delight than to turn within and find sincerity.
    Mencius
    Philosophy
  18. Before joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure are issued, that is called the Mean; when issued and all hit due measure, that is called Harmony.
    The Doctrine of the Mean
    Order
  19. Nothing is miserable unless you think it so.
    Boethius
    Judgment
  20. What a person is contributes more to his happiness than what he has.
    Arthur Schopenhauer
    Happiness
  21. It is better to be a human being dissatisfied than a pig satisfied.
    John Stuart Mill
    Happiness
  22. There is no greater pain than to recall happy times in misery.
    Dante Alighieri
    Memory
  23. Luck can intervene between a person and the living of the good human life.
    Martha Nussbaum
    Fate
  24. The capabilities approach asks not only about people's total or average well-being but about what each person is able to do and to be.
    Martha Nussbaum
    Freedom
  25. The excellent city is the one in which people cooperate toward the things by which true happiness is attained.
    Al-Farabi
    Happiness
  26. Happiness is the good desired for its own sake; it is never desired for the sake of something else.
    Al-Farabi
    Happiness
  27. Political science inquires into the kinds of voluntary actions and ways of life, and into the happiness that is the end of the human being.
    Al-Farabi
    Politics
